title: 1812 Prairie's porch arch, transom and stair newels to the photograph
items: The porch arch of 1812 Prairie now has the half-elliptical head Albert Levy's photograph shows, flat over the crown, turned in a narrow moulded ring of light stone that runs down both jambs. Under its fanlight is a heavy moulded transom beam, and two narrow columns of small panes divide the fanlight, one over the doors' meeting and one over the pier. The stair's north cheek now flares out as it sweeps down, and each cheek ends in a carved newel under a cap with a turned knob. The mouldings, the knob and the carving are reconstructed; the arch's south jamb against the projection is still to come.
